items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines local maximum of a surface.

a place on a curved two variable graph higher than every nearby place
the term of such an expression that carries no i
a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines conjugate.
o: the number obtained by adding the products of corresponding components of two ordered triples
the whole family of expressions whose derivatives equal the given one, written with an arbitrary number
the expression obtained by reversing the sign of the i term
one of the simpler ratios into which a proper algebraic ratio is split before integrating
items.s: conjugate: the expression obtained by reversing the sign of the i term. The other options describe indefinite integral, partial fraction, dot product.

items.q: Which of the following best describes sequence?
o: an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers
a list in which each term after the first is obtained by adding a fixed number
the use of the tangent value to approximate the output near a chosen input
a quantity of size one pointing along a stated direction
items.s: sequence: an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers. The other options describe linear estimate, arithmetic progression, unit vector.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines vector.
o: the unknown number added when a whole family of primitives is written down
the rate of change with respect to one variable while the others are held fixed
the straight edge that touches a curve at one place and shares its gradient there
a quantity with both size and direction
items.s: vector: a quantity with both size and direction. The other options describe arbitrary constant, partial derivative, tangent line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes saddle point?
o: the component of a unit triple along one of the coordinate axes
a stationary place on a surface that is a rise in one direction and a fall in another
the angle that the line from the origin to the representing point makes with the positive real axis
a gap in a graph where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
items.s: saddle point: a stationary place on a surface that is a rise in one direction and a fall in another. The other options describe removable break, direction cosine, argument.

absolute convergence

o: the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers
a stationary point where the curve stops falling and starts rising
a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling
an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers
items.s: series: the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers. The other options describe minimum place, maximum place, sequence.

the number obtained as the difference of a primitive evaluated at the upper and at the lower end
the number given by the determinant of three ordered triples taken as rows, equal to the volume they span
an expression whose own derivative is the given one

the stated value of the unknown at a chosen point, used to fix the arbitrary numbers
the square root of the sum of the squares of the three components
the accumulated total divided by the length of the range, for a continuous quantity

an expression whose own derivative is the given one

the expression obtained by reversing the sign of the i term

the rule for differentiating a composition, multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative

the rate of change with respect to one variable while the others are held fixed
the ordered triple whose components are the two by two determinants of the paired components

the square root of the sum of the squares of the three components
the small change in the output produced by small changes in all the inputs together
the instantaneous rate at which one quantity changes with respect to another

a numerical approximation built from parabolas drawn through successive triples of points
the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated
a relation containing an unknown function together with one or more of its rates of change
items.s: removable break: a gap in a graph where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there. The other options describe differential equation, limits of integration, Simpson estimate.

a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that uses the middle value of each strip
the expression that differentiates a multiplication as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first
a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that joins successive points by straight lines

a quantity with both size and direction

the expression for the derivative of a ratio of two functions, built from their derivatives and the square of the lower one

unit vector
magnitude of a triple

the solid content swept out when a plane region is turned about an axis

complex number
argument

items.q: Which statement correctly defines infinite break?
o: a gap where the output grows without bound as the input nears the stated place
a quantity of size one pointing along a stated direction
the rate of change with respect to one variable while the others are held fixed
the expression for the derivative of a ratio of two functions, built from their derivatives and the square of the lower one
items.s: infinite break: a gap where the output grows without bound as the input nears the stated place. The other options describe partial derivative, quotient formula, unit vector.

items.q: Which term is described by “the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated”?
o: trapezium estimate
midpoint estimate
limits of integration
volume of revolution
items.s: limits of integration is the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated.

items.q: area between two curves may be defined as
o: a gap in a graph where the two one sided approach values exist but are not equal
the accumulated difference of the upper and the lower values over a stated range
a place on a curved two variable graph higher than every nearby place
the accumulated total divided by the length of the range, for a continuous quantity
items.s: area between two curves: the accumulated difference of the upper and the lower values over a stated range. The other options describe jump break, local maximum of a surface, mean value over an interval.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines product formula.
o: a stationary point where the curve stops falling and starts rising
the writing of such an expression as a size times a cosine plus i sine of an angle
the expression that differentiates a multiplication as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first
the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers
items.s: product formula: the expression that differentiates a multiplication as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first. The other options describe minimum place, polar form, series.

items.q: limits of integration may be defined as
o: the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated
a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that uses the middle value of each strip
the solid content swept out when a plane region is turned about an axis
the rate of change with respect to one variable while the others are held fixed
items.s: limits of integration: the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated. The other options describe volume of revolution, midpoint estimate, partial derivative.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines directional derivative?
o: the rate of change along a stated unit direction
the distance of the point representing the expression from the origin
the stated value of the unknown at a chosen point, used to fix the arbitrary numbers
the rank of the highest rate of change appearing in the relation
items.s: directional derivative: the rate of change along a stated unit direction. The other options describe initial condition, modulus, order of an equation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes maximum place?
o: the rank of the highest rate of change appearing in the relation
the stated value of the unknown at a chosen point, used to fix the arbitrary numbers
the term of such an expression that carries no i
a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling
items.s: maximum place: a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling. The other options describe initial condition, real part, order of an equation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes integration by substitution?
o: an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers
the technique of changing the variable so that an awkward expression becomes a standard form
the solid content swept out when a plane region is turned about an axis
a numerical approximation built from parabolas drawn through successive triples of points
items.s: integration by substitution: the technique of changing the variable so that an awkward expression becomes a standard form. The other options describe sequence, Simpson estimate, volume of revolution.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines implicit method.
o: the number obtained by adding the products of corresponding components of two ordered triples
the technique of finding a gradient from an equation in which the two variables are mixed and not separated
the angle that the line from the origin to the representing point makes with the positive real axis
the power of the scaling factor by which the value is multiplied when all inputs are scaled
items.s: implicit method: the technique of finding a gradient from an equation in which the two variables are mixed and not separated. The other options describe dot product, argument, degree of homogeneity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines continuity at a place?
o: the multiplier that turns the left side of a first order relation into the exact rate of change of a product
the property that the output value equals both one sided approach values at that input
a quantity with size only and no direction
the rate of change along a stated unit direction
items.s: continuity at a place: the property that the output value equals both one sided approach values at that input. The other options describe integrating factor, scalar, directional derivative.

items.q: maximum place may be defined as
o: a quantity of size one pointing along a stated direction
the technique of finding a gradient as the ratio of the two rates of change when both vary with a third quantity
a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling
the expression that differentiates a multiplication as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first
items.s: maximum place: a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling. The other options describe parametric method, unit vector, product formula.

items.q: Which term is described by “a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling”?
o: second derivative check
normal line
maximum place
stationary place
items.s: maximum place is a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines modulus?
o: the property that the total of the sizes of the terms is finite
the distance of the point representing the expression from the origin
the number given by the determinant of three ordered triples taken as rows, equal to the volume they span
a quantity of size one pointing along a stated direction
items.s: modulus: the distance of the point representing the expression from the origin. The other options describe scalar triple product, unit vector, absolute convergence.

items.q: The statement “the ordered triple whose components are the two by two determinants of the paired components” describes which of the following?
o: cross product
dot product
magnitude of a triple
unit vector
items.s: cross product is the ordered triple whose components are the two by two determinants of the paired components.

items.q: All of the following belong to First order differential equations EXCEPT
o: second derivative check
order of an equation
differential equation
separable equation
items.s: Every other option belongs to First order differential equations. “second derivative check” belongs to Applications of differentiation, not First order differential equations.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines arithmetic progression.
o: the number obtained by adding the products of corresponding components of two ordered triples
the stated value of the unknown at a chosen point, used to fix the arbitrary numbers
a list in which each term after the first is obtained by adding a fixed number
the result of differentiating first with respect to one variable and then with respect to another
items.s: arithmetic progression: a list in which each term after the first is obtained by adding a fixed number. The other options describe dot product, mixed second derivative, initial condition.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines improper integral?
o: the accumulated total divided by the length of the range, for a continuous quantity
an accumulated total taken over an unbounded range or up to a place where the integrand blows up
an answer with the arbitrary numbers fixed by stated conditions
one of the simpler ratios into which a proper algebraic ratio is split before integrating
items.s: improper integral: an accumulated total taken over an unbounded range or up to a place where the integrand blows up. The other options describe particular solution, mean value over an interval, partial fraction.

items.q: improper integral may be defined as
o: the technique of taking natural logs of both sides before differentiating a product of powers
the expression that differentiates a multiplication as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first
an accumulated total taken over an unbounded range or up to a place where the integrand blows up
the term of such an expression that carries no i
items.s: improper integral: an accumulated total taken over an unbounded range or up to a place where the integrand blows up. The other options describe product formula, logarithmic method, real part.

items.q: Given y = (x + 2)(x^2 + 2), find dy/dx at x = 1.
items.s: The product formula gives 3x^2 + 4x + 2, so at x = 1 the value is 9.

items.q: Find the gradient of the tangent to the curve y = x^3 - 5x at the point where x = 2.
items.s: dy/dx = 3x^2 - 5, so at x = 2 the gradient is 7.

items.q: Evaluate the definite integral of 3x^4 + 1 with respect to x from x = 0 to x = 3.
items.s: The primitive is 3x^5/5 + 1x, so the value is 148.8.

items.q: An arithmetic progression has first term 3 and common difference 5. Find the sum of the first 9 terms.
items.s: The sum is 9/2 x (2 x 3 + 8 x 5) = 207.

items.q: A geometric progression has first term 3 and common ratio 2. Find the sum of the first 6 terms.
Given f(x, y) = 2x^2 y + 3y^3, find the partial derivative of f with respect to x at the point (2, 2).
items.s: The x derivative is 4xy, which at (2, 2) equals 16.

items.q: A quantity y satisfies dy/dt = 0.3y with y = 100 when t = 0. Find y when t = 3.
items.s: The solution is y = 100e^(0.3t), so at t = 3, y = 246.

items.q: Find the dot product of the vectors (2, -2, 5) and (3, 4, -2).
items.s: Multiplying matching components and adding gives -12.

items.q: Find the real part of the product (1 + 5i)(2 + 1i).
items.s: The real part is 1 x 2 - 5 x 1 = -3.

items.q: Evaluate the limit of (x^2 - 16)/(x - 4) as x tends to 4.
items.s: Factorising gives (x + 4), so the limit is 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Evaluate the limit of (x^3 - 343)/(x - 7) as x tends to 7.
items.s: The quotient simplifies to x^2 + 7x + 49, so at x = 7 the value is 147.

items.q: Given y = 6x^2 + x, find dy/dx at x = 1.
items.s: dy/dx = 12x^1 + 1, so at x = 1 the value is 13.

items.q: Given y = (x + 2)/(x + 5), find dy/dx at x = 3.
items.s: dy/dx = (5 - 2)/(x + 5)^2 = 3/64, so at x = 3 the value is 0.0469.

items.q: Given y = (3x + 3)^4, find dy/dx at x = 2.
items.s: dy/dx = 4 x 3 x (3x + 3)^3, so at x = 2 the value is 8748.

items.q: The curve y = x^2 - 6x + 5 has one stationary point. Find the x coordinate of that point.
items.s: dy/dx = 2x + -6, which is zero at x = 3.

items.q: The radius of a circle increases at 1.5 cm per second. Taking pi as 3.142, find the rate at which the area increases, in square centimetres per second, at the instant when the radius is 3 cm.
Use the tangent approximation at x = 2 to estimate (2.05)^3.
items.s: The change is about 3 x 2^2 x 0.05 = 0.6, added to 2^3 = 8, giving 8.6.

items.q: Evaluate the integral of (4x + 2)^2 with respect to x from x = 0 to x = 2.
items.s: The primitive is (4x + 2)^3/12, so the value is 82.67.

items.q: Evaluate the integral of x times e^(3x) with respect to x from x = 0 to x = 1.
items.s: Integrating by parts gives the value 4.57.

items.q: The first term of an arithmetic progression is 5 and the common difference is 4. Find the 10th term.
items.s: The 10th term is 5 + 9 x 4 = 41.

items.q: Find the sum to infinity of the geometric progression with first term 8 and common ratio 1/5.
Find the coefficient of x^2 in the expansion of (1 + 2x)^7.
items.s: The term is C(7, 2) x 2^2 x x^2 = 84.

items.q: Find the coefficient of x^2 in the Maclaurin expansion of e^(4x).
items.s: The x^2 term is (4 x)^2/2, so the coefficient is 8.

items.q: Given f(x, y) = 2x^2 y^3, find the mixed second derivative taken first in x then in y, at the point (1, 2).
items.s: Differentiating in x gives 4xy^3, then in y gives 12xy^2, which at (1, 2) is 48.

items.q: A quantity y satisfies dy/dt = -0.1y with y = 500 when t = 0. Find y when t = 4.
items.s: The solution is y = 500e^(-0.1t), so at t = 4, y = 335.2.

items.q: Find the magnitude of the cross product of the vectors (2, 3, 0) and (0, 2, 2).
items.s: The cross product is (6, -4, 4), whose magnitude is 8.25.

items.q: Find the limit of the sequence (4n + 7)/(1n + 13) as n tends to infinity.
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 4/1, so the limit is 4.

items.q: Given y = (x + 3)(x^2 + 3), find dy/dx at x = 2.
items.s: The product formula gives 3x^2 + 6x + 3, so at x = 2 the value is 27.

items.q: Find the gradient of the tangent to the curve y = x^3 - 4x at the point where x = 1.
items.s: dy/dx = 3x^2 - 4, so at x = 1 the gradient is -1.

items.q: Evaluate the definite integral of 4x^2 + 3 with respect to x from x = 0 to x = 1.
items.s: The primitive is 4x^3/3 + 3x, so the value is 4.33.

items.q: An arithmetic progression has first term 6 and common difference 2. Find the sum of the first 10 terms.
items.s: The sum is 10/2 x (2 x 6 + 9 x 2) = 150.

items.q: A geometric progression has first term 4 and common ratio 2. Find the sum of the first 5 terms.
Given f(x, y) = 4x^2 y + 2y^3, find the partial derivative of f with respect to x at the point (1, 4).
items.s: The x derivative is 8xy, which at (1, 4) equals 32.

items.q: A quantity y satisfies dy/dt = 0.1y with y = 40 when t = 0. Find y when t = 3.
items.s: The solution is y = 40e^(0.1t), so at t = 3, y = 53.99.

items.q: Find the dot product of the vectors (2, 1, 3) and (4, 3, 1).
items.s: Multiplying matching components and adding gives 14.

items.q: Evaluate the limit of (x^3 - 64)/(x - 4) as x tends to 4.
items.s: The quotient simplifies to x^2 + 4x + 16, so at x = 4 the value is 48.

items.q: Evaluate the limit of sin(4x)/x as x tends to zero.
items.s: Since sin(u)/u tends to one, the quotient tends to 4 multiplied by one, giving 4.

items.q: Given y = 4x^4 + 2x, find dy/dx at x = 1.
items.s: dy/dx = 16x^3 + 2, so at x = 1 the value is 18.

items.q: Given y = (4x + 2)^4, find dy/dx at x = 1.
items.s: dy/dx = 4 x 4 x (4x + 2)^3, so at x = 1 the value is 3456.

items.q: Given y = 2x^3 + 6x^2 + 7x, find the second derivative at x = 2.
items.s: The second derivative is 12x + 12, so at x = 2 the value is 36.

items.q: The curve y = x^2 + 4x + 3 has one stationary point. Find the x coordinate of that point.
items.s: dy/dx = 2x + 4, which is zero at x = -2.

items.q: The curve y = -3x^2 + 6x + 5 has a maximum point. Find the largest value of y on the curve.
items.s: The turning value is at x = 1 and substituting gives y = 8.

items.q: The radius of a circle increases at 2.5 cm per second. Taking pi as 3.142, find the rate at which the area increases, in square centimetres per second, at the instant when the radius is 4 cm.
Use the tangent approximation at x = 2 to estimate (2.05)^2.
items.s: The change is about 2 x 2^1 x 0.05 = 0.2, added to 2^2 = 4, giving 4.2.

items.q: Evaluate the integral of (3x + 2)^2 with respect to x from x = 0 to x = 1.
items.s: The primitive is (3x + 2)^3/9, so the value is 13.

items.q: Find the area enclosed between the line y = 3x and the curve y = x^2.
items.s: The limits are x = 0 and x = 3, and the area is 3^3/6 = 4.5.

items.q: The first term of an arithmetic progression is 2 and the common difference is 5. Find the 10th term.
items.s: The 10th term is 2 + 9 x 5 = 47.

items.q: Find the sum to infinity of the geometric progression with first term 9 and common ratio 1/5.
Find the coefficient of x^2 in the expansion of (1 + 4x)^4.
items.s: The term is C(4, 2) x 4^2 x x^2 = 96.

items.q: Find the coefficient of x^2 in the Maclaurin expansion of e^(2x).
items.s: The x^2 term is (2 x)^2/2, so the coefficient is 2.

items.q: Given f(x, y) = 3x^2 y^3, find the mixed second derivative taken first in x then in y, at the point (1, 1).
items.s: Differentiating in x gives 6xy^3, then in y gives 18xy^2, which at (1, 1) is 18.

items.q: A quantity y satisfies dy/dt = -0.1y with y = 800 when t = 0. Find y when t = 2.
items.s: The solution is y = 800e^(-0.1t), so at t = 2, y = 655.

items.q: Find the magnitude of the cross product of the vectors (4, 2, 0) and (0, 3, 2).
items.s: The cross product is (4, -8, 12), whose magnitude is 14.97.

items.q: Find the modulus of the complex number 3 + 4i.
items.s: The modulus is the square root of 25, which is 5.

items.q: Find the argument, in degrees, of the complex number +1 + 1i.
items.s: The point is equally far from both axes, so the argument is 45 degrees.

items.q: Find the limit of the sequence (3n + 3)/(5n + 13) as n tends to infinity.
items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 3/5, so the limit is 0.6.

items.q: Given y = (x + 3)(x^2 + 5), find dy/dx at x = 2.
items.s: The product formula gives 3x^2 + 6x + 5, so at x = 2 the value is 29.

items.q: Evaluate the definite integral of 3x^3 + 2 with respect to x from x = 0 to x = 2.
items.s: The primitive is 3x^4/4 + 2x, so the value is 16.

items.q: An arithmetic progression has first term 6 and common difference 4. Find the sum of the first 9 terms.
items.s: The sum is 9/2 x (2 x 6 + 8 x 4) = 198.

items.q: A geometric progression has first term 2 and common ratio 3. Find the sum of the first 5 terms.
The best definition of scalar among these is
o: the square root of the sum of the squares of the three components
a quantity of size one pointing along a stated direction
the ordered triple whose components are the two by two determinants of the paired components
a quantity with size only and no direction
items.s: scalar: a quantity with size only and no direction. The other options describe cross product, magnitude of a triple, unit vector.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an expression whose own derivative is the given one”
o: antiderivative
integration by parts
definite integral
partial fraction
items.s: antiderivative is an expression whose own derivative is the given one.

items.q: logarithmic method is best described as
o: the rule for differentiating a composition, multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative
the expression that differentiates a multiplication as first times derivative of second plus second times derivative of first
the technique of taking natural logs of both sides before differentiating a product of powers
the technique of finding a gradient as the ratio of the two rates of change when both vary with a third quantity
items.s: logarithmic method: the technique of taking natural logs of both sides before differentiating a product of powers. The other options describe chain formula, parametric method, product formula.

items.q: In this course, partial fraction refers to
o: the unknown number added when a whole family of primitives is written down
the technique that rewrites an integral of a product using one factor differentiated and the other integrated
one of the simpler ratios into which a proper algebraic ratio is split before integrating
the number obtained as the difference of a primitive evaluated at the upper and at the lower end
items.s: partial fraction: one of the simpler ratios into which a proper algebraic ratio is split before integrating. The other options describe arbitrary constant, integration by parts, definite integral.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the power of the scaling factor by which the value is multiplied when all inputs are scaled”
o: local maximum of a surface
partial derivative
directional derivative
degree of homogeneity
items.s: degree of homogeneity is the power of the scaling factor by which the value is multiplied when all inputs are scaled.

items.q: The statement “a place on a curved two variable graph higher than every nearby place” describes which of the following?
o: local maximum of a surface
total differential
directional derivative
saddle point
items.s: local maximum of a surface is a place on a curved two variable graph higher than every nearby place.

items.q: The statement “a gap where the output grows without bound as the input nears the stated place” describes which of the following?
o: removable break
jump break
infinite break
sandwich principle
items.s: infinite break is a gap where the output grows without bound as the input nears the stated place.

items.q: The best definition of volume of revolution among these is
o: a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that joins successive points by straight lines
a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that uses the middle value of each strip
the solid content swept out when a plane region is turned about an axis
the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated
items.s: volume of revolution: the solid content swept out when a plane region is turned about an axis. The other options describe limits of integration, midpoint estimate, trapezium estimate.

items.q: In this course, integrating factor refers to
o: the multiplier that turns the left side of a first order relation into the exact rate of change of a product
the rank of the highest rate of change appearing in the relation
a relation containing an unknown function together with one or more of its rates of change
a relation in which the unknown and its rates of change appear only to the first power and are never multiplied together
items.s: integrating factor: the multiplier that turns the left side of a first order relation into the exact rate of change of a product. The other options describe order of an equation, differential equation, linear equation.

items.q: total differential is best described as
o: the small change in the output produced by small changes in all the inputs together
the rate of change along a stated unit direction
a place on a curved two variable graph higher than every nearby place
the result of differentiating first with respect to one variable and then with respect to another
items.s: total differential: the small change in the output produced by small changes in all the inputs together. The other options describe mixed second derivative, directional derivative, local maximum of a surface.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what trapezium estimate means.
o: a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that uses the middle value of each strip
the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated
a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that joins successive points by straight lines
an accumulated total that counts regions below the axis as negative
items.s: trapezium estimate: a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that joins successive points by straight lines. The other options describe signed area, midpoint estimate, limits of integration.

items.q: The best definition of mean value over an interval among these is
o: the solid content swept out when a plane region is turned about an axis
the lower and upper values between which a total is accumulated
the accumulated total divided by the length of the range, for a continuous quantity
an accumulated total that counts regions below the axis as negative
items.s: mean value over an interval: the accumulated total divided by the length of the range, for a continuous quantity. The other options describe limits of integration, signed area, volume of revolution.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the writing of such an expression as a size times a cosine plus i sine of an angle”
o: de Moivre statement
conjugate
polar form
complex number
items.s: polar form is the writing of such an expression as a size times a cosine plus i sine of an angle.

items.q: linear estimate is best described as
o: the straight edge that touches a curve at one place and shares its gradient there
the use of the tangent value to approximate the output near a chosen input
how quickly one quantity alters with respect to another
a stationary point where the curve stops rising and starts falling
items.s: linear estimate: the use of the tangent value to approximate the output near a chosen input. The other options describe maximum place, rate of change, tangent line.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what series means.
o: an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers
the fixed number multiplied to move from one term to the next in a multiplicative list
the fixed number added to move from one term to the next in an additive list
the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers
items.s: series: the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers. The other options describe sequence, common difference, common ratio.

items.q: The statement “the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers” describes which of the following?
o: common difference
arithmetic progression
geometric progression
series
items.s: series is the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers.

items.q: The statement “a stationary point where the curve stops falling and starts rising” describes which of the following?
o: stationary place
minimum place
second derivative check
point of inflexion
items.s: minimum place is a stationary point where the curve stops falling and starts rising.

items.q: The best definition of directional derivative among these is
o: the small change in the output produced by small changes in all the inputs together
the rate of change along a stated unit direction
the rate of change with respect to one variable while the others are held fixed
the result of differentiating first with respect to one variable and then with respect to another
items.s: directional derivative: the rate of change along a stated unit direction. The other options describe total differential, mixed second derivative, partial derivative.

items.q: The best definition of removable break among these is
o: the statement that a quantity trapped between two others sharing a common bound must itself tend to that bound
a gap in a graph where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there
the number that the output tends to as the input comes up towards a place from above
the number that the output tends to as the input comes down towards a place from below
items.s: removable break: a gap in a graph where the two sided approach value exists but differs from the value taken there. The other options describe left hand approach value, sandwich principle, right hand approach value.

items.q: improper integral is best described as
o: an accumulated total taken over an unbounded range or up to a place where the integrand blows up
the whole family of expressions whose derivatives equal the given one, written with an arbitrary number
the number obtained as the difference of a primitive evaluated at the upper and at the lower end
the unknown number added when a whole family of primitives is written down
items.s: improper integral: an accumulated total taken over an unbounded range or up to a place where the integrand blows up. The other options describe indefinite integral, arbitrary constant, definite integral.

items.q: The statement “the number obtained as the difference of a primitive evaluated at the upper and at the lower end” describes which of the following?
o: indefinite integral
antiderivative
partial fraction
definite integral
items.s: definite integral is the number obtained as the difference of a primitive evaluated at the upper and at the lower end.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the instantaneous rate at which one quantity changes with respect to another”
o: higher derivative
derivative
logarithmic method
product formula
items.s: derivative is the instantaneous rate at which one quantity changes with respect to another.

items.q: In this course, area between two curves refers to
o: the accumulated total divided by the length of the range, for a continuous quantity
an accumulated total that counts regions below the axis as negative
a numerical approximation of an accumulated total that joins successive points by straight lines
the accumulated difference of the upper and the lower values over a stated range
items.s: area between two curves: the accumulated difference of the upper and the lower values over a stated range. The other options describe signed area, trapezium estimate, mean value over an interval.

items.q: The best definition of series among these is
o: the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers
the property that the total of the sizes of the terms is finite
an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers
a list in which each term after the first is obtained by multiplying by a fixed number
items.s: series: the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers. The other options describe absolute convergence, geometric progression, sequence.

items.q: The statement “the fixed number added to move from one term to the next in an additive list” describes which of the following?
o: common ratio
series
common difference
geometric progression
items.s: common difference is the fixed number added to move from one term to the next in an additive list.

items.q: The best definition of degree of homogeneity among these is
o: a stationary place on a surface that is a rise in one direction and a fall in another
the result of differentiating first with respect to one variable and then with respect to another
the power of the scaling factor by which the value is multiplied when all inputs are scaled
the rate of change along a stated unit direction
items.s: degree of homogeneity: the power of the scaling factor by which the value is multiplied when all inputs are scaled. The other options describe directional derivative, mixed second derivative, saddle point.

items.q: The best definition of Maclaurin expansion among these is
o: an ordered list of numbers indexed by the counting numbers
the total obtained by adding the terms of an ordered list of numbers
the power series of an expression about zero
the total of the first stated number of terms of a list
items.s: Maclaurin expansion: the power series of an expression about zero. The other options describe partial sum, sequence, series.

items.q: In this course, dot product refers to
o: the square root of the sum of the squares of the three components
the ordered triple whose components are the two by two determinants of the paired components
a quantity of size one pointing along a stated direction
the number obtained by adding the products of corresponding components of two ordered triples
items.s: dot product: the number obtained by adding the products of corresponding components of two ordered triples. The other options describe unit vector, cross product, magnitude of a triple.

items.q: The statement “an answer with the arbitrary numbers fixed by stated conditions” describes which of the following?
o: general solution
linear equation
order of an equation

items.s: Differentiating in x gives 6xy^3, then in y gives 18xy^2, which at (2, 3) is 324.

items.s: The cross product is (3, -4, 8), whose magnitude is 9.43.

items.s: Dividing every term by n leaves 5/1, so the limit is 5.

items.s: The quotient simplifies to x^2 + 6x + 36, so at x = 6 the value is 108.

items.s: dy/dx = 9x^2 + 3, so at x = 1 the value is 12.

items.s: The product formula gives 3x^2 + 2x + 3, so at x = 2 the value is 19.

items.q: Given y = (3x + 2)^5, find dy/dx at x = 2.

items.s: Differentiating in x gives 4xy^3, then in y gives 12xy^2, which at (1, 3) is 108.
